newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Woodside says receives Gorgon gas plan.
newsitem.headline: Woodside says receives Gorgon gas plan.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd, operator of the North West Shelf oil and gas project offshore Western Australia, said on Friday it had received a joint development proposal from the operator of the neighbouring Gorgon gas prospect.

"Woodside, on behalf of the North West Shelf participants welcomed the Gorgon proposal on the basis that it may provide an opportunity to increase LNG (liquefied natural gas) capacity on the Burrup (Peninsula) beyond the two train expansion which is currently under discussion with the North West Shelf Project's existing Japanese LNG customers," Woodside said.
The Gorgon proposal calls for construction of two more LNG trains tapping Gorgon gas reserves and the North West Shelf Project's infrastructure, Woodside said.

This could increase the LNG capacity of the Burrup Peninsula to a possible 21 million tonnes a year from 14.5 million, significantly increasing Australia's presence in the international LNG market, Woodside said.

The Shelf project had had a highly successful exploration and appraisal programme in 1996 and as a result the partners were confident that the project's acreage contained the reserves required for its current LNG expansion plans, Woodside said.

"These expansion plans will not be affected by the proposal from the Gorgon participants because third party gas is not required for trains four and five, which will deliver a further seven million tonnes of LNG per annum to Japan," it said.
The integration of the Gorgon proposal with the North West Shelf will require the resolution of technical and commercial issues, Woodside said.
"The key to success will be to find an approach which delivers value to all participants," it said.

The equal North West Shelf partners are The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Ltd, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui and Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Inc, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside.
The North West Shelf project's LNG plant has a capacity of 7.5 million tonnes a year.
The Gorgon partners are Mobil Corp, with a one-seventh stake, and Texaco, Chevron and Royal Dutch/Shell, each with a two-sevenths stake.
